driver.do_not_ask_when: slot is empty but impact is low
driver.uncertainty: derived from completeness (0-100) and confidence (see confidence below)
driver.impact: how much this slot changes the shape/cost of the plan; estimated using the product context (context/*.md)
driver.impact_is_dynamic: impact_default is only a BASELINE. Raise a slot's impact above its default when the request or context names a driver for it (a slot's impact_signals list the triggers). A regulated audience, a two-sided market, or a channel with a legal regime (unsolicited-contact rules) makes channels and offer high-impact, whatever their default.

confidence.explicit: the requester committed to this. A third party's own word (a client, a stakeholder) always qualifies. With no third party -- a solo builder describing their own idea -- ONLY their own intent qualifies: what they want, will or will not build, will spend, have decided. Their unconfirmed belief about the world (what an audience wants, what a channel yields, what the market will bear) is NEVER explicit, no matter how confidently it is stated -- grade it inferred or testable instead.
confidence.inferred: deduced by you, OR the requester's own unconfirmed belief about the world -- an assumption to confirm before it drives the plan.
confidence.empty: unknown, and answerable by asking the person in front of you.
confidence.testable: unknown, and NOT answerable by asking -- only a real test or experiment would settle it. This is the default state of a half-formed go-to-market idea, not an edge case: 'will anyone pay for this' is rarely answerable by conversation alone. Requires test_plan naming what would settle it, or the slot is refused. Does not block readiness: a named test still to run is compatible with 'precise enough to act on'.

pillars.why: Why? The objective, its clock, and the metric that tells you it worked.
pillars.what: What? Who this is for, what already reaches them, and what is offered.
pillars.how: How? Channels, economics, and the resources actually available.
pillars.validate: Validation. How this is measured, and the thresholds that trigger a decision.

slots.label: Objective
slots.probe: What is the one outcome this is meant to achieve, and by when?

slots.label: Success metric
slots.probe: What is the leading indicator, separate from the goal -- and what does its counting rule deliberately exclude?

slots.label: Ideal customer profile
slots.probe: Who is this for, narrowly enough that you could name someone it is NOT for?

slots.label: Existing distribution
slots.probe: What audience, relationship or surface already exists -- a list, a community, a partner, a following?
slots.impact_signals: -> the single biggest determinant of which channels are even viable; a request naming no existing distribution raises channels' impact.

slots.label: Offer
slots.probe: What is given, to whom, on what terms?
slots.impact_signals: -> high when the offer targets a two-sided market or a regulated audience -- a different build than the same word suggests generically.

slots.label: Channels
slots.probe: What are the candidate routes to the audience, and which does existing distribution actually support?
slots.impact_signals: -> high when a candidate channel carries a legal regime (unsolicited-contact rules, a platform policy) or the audience is regulated.

slots.label: Unit economics
slots.probe: What is a customer worth, and over what period -- what turns a threshold from an assertion into a derivation?

slots.label: Capacity
slots.probe: How many hours per week are actually available, and for how many weeks?
slots.impact_signals: -> the binding constraint: a plan that does not fit the hours available is not a plan, whatever the budget says.

slots.label: Budget
slots.probe: How much money is available, and is it committed or conditional on an early result?

slots.label: Horizon
slots.probe: What is the clock the objective runs on -- when does this get judged?

slots.label: Instrumentation
slots.probe: How is any of this actually measured, and what about it is not measurable at all?

slots.label: Decision thresholds
slots.probe: At what result does this continue, change, or stop -- 'at X, do Y'?
